answer: Mechanism: metered-line binding with sealed keys. Enrollment ships a sealed key module — a pearl a few millimeters across — whose private half cannot be read without destroying it. Each identity must also be bound to three independently metered last-mile lines at distinct addresses, each with its own utility account and phase signature. A juniper sweep re-reads those signatures hourly, revoking any identity whose key answers from a mismatched round-trip delay. The trellis check drops identities that share a line.
